reason: About 58% of the weight comes from bills that cut fees and levies on employing foreign workers (rows 1-3, 9, 12, 13, 24: nursing, hotels, general). Most of the rest are permit and visa bills (nursing permits, extensions, temporary replacement workers, bereaved families). All of them make it cheaper or easier to bring foreign workers in. The statement asks about exactly that trade-off: fewer foreign workers against higher costs, and it already names the price (elderly care, construction, agriculture), which is why the fee-cut bills were proposed. A voter who agrees would oppose these bills, so the key (agree = less inflow) fits. The bills against transferring money abroad by infiltrators or foreign nationals (rows 4, 5, 16; about 15% of the weight) are mainly about asylum seekers and remittances, not the size of the foreign workforce, so they are only loosely on topic. The Palestinian work-permit bills (rows 7, 10) are a related labor-inflow question with little weight. Neither group justifies a rewrite.
